newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pannon-Flax pays dividend, sees profit up.
newsitem.headline: Pannon-Flax pays dividend, sees profit up.

text.p: Hungarian textiles industrial company Pannon-Flax will pay a five percent dividend on its 1996 earnings following shareholders' approval on Friday, making the first payout since 1991.
"The board proposed to pay dividend to shareholders even though we would need these funds for development," Chairman and CEO Etelka Peimel told shareholders at the company's annual general meeting.
Dividend payouts will start on May 29.
In 1996 the company posted an unconsolidated pre-tax profit of 82.7 million forints and after-tax profit of 71.1 million on net sales of 2.37 billion forints.
The company's results exceeded not only the pre-tax of 32.4 million forints in 1995 but also the 1996 plan of 61 million forints.
The company's unconsolidated net sales rose to 2.37 billion forints in 1996 from 1.77 billion in 1995 but within total sales, exports remained below the 1995 figures.
In 1997, the company plans to boost its pre-tax profit to 110 million forints while sales are seen increasing to 3.11 billion forints.
"I think we have the base for a more profitable operation," Peimel said.

"Signs of an economic recovery can be seen, there is an opportunity to increase the number of clients on both domestic and export markets, while inflation and interest rates are declining," Pannon-Flax said in its 1997 business plan.
Peimel said last year's investments of 91.3 million forints and this year's planned investment of at least 118.2 million forints will bolster sales.
Pending sources, the company will have to invest another nearly 100 million forints for computerised product planning and the securement of its own steam supply.
One possible way of financing was a capital increase on which the company has not yet decided.
